title: AI Megacap Earnings Hangover (Alphabet, Palantir, Amazon)
summary: Gotrade News - Alphabet (GOOGL) shares fell 13% in one session after its October 28 third-quarter report showed free cash flow turning negative, erasing
body_markdown:
Palantir guided fourth-quarter revenue to $2.649 billion to $2.653 billion and raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $8.530 billion to $8.534 billion, which the company put at 91% growth, according to its[third-quarter release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000045/a2026q3ex991pressrelease.htm) . “Our U.S. commercial revenue has surpassed our U.S. government revenue for the first time in our company's history,” chief executive Alexander Karp said in the release. CNBC reported US government revenue rose 96% to $953 million.


## Why Did Alphabet (GOOGL) Stock Fall 13%?


Parts of the report disappointed investors, The Motley Fool reported, including cash flow: free cash flow came in at negative $9.1 billion, per Alphabet's[third-quarter release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm) , against analysts' estimates of $2.7 billion. The Motley Fool also noted that Alphabet kept its 2026 capital expenditure forecast unchanged at $195 billion to $205 billion, and that investors are concerned AI growth may not justify current spending levels.


The release showed $51.4 billion of purchases of property and equipment in the quarter, while Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion. Diluted EPS of $2.12 fell short of expectations of about $3.00, and net income dropped 25%, partly due to an $8.7 billion loss on equity investments, according to[XTB](https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/news-and-research/alphabet-disappoints-wall-street-despite-record-results-shares-plunge-over-8-and-test-300) . Chief executive Sundar Pichai said in the release that Alphabet is “now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate.”


Estimates of the market value lost vary:[The National News Desk](https://okcfox.com/news/nation-world/googles-parent-company-suffers-largest-stock-market-wipeout-ever-artificial-intelligence-shareholders) put it at $482 billion, against about $500 billion in The Motley Fool's count. Susannah Streeter of Wealth Club told the Daily Mail, as reported by The National News Desk, that “the days of rewarding companies simply for announcing massive AI investments have faded fast.” She added, “The AI opportunity remains enormous, but the market is no longer prepared to give companies a blank check to pursue it.”
